Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. I can get you the CSV and diagram; a couple notes up front so expectations align:

- Hosted API egress: we publish a stable set of NAT IP ranges for customer allowlisting. For high-throughput tenants we sometimes use ephemeral SNAT ranges that rotate on a weekly cadence; when rotation happens we publish a 72-hour heads-up window.
- Private endpoint (VPC endpoint / PrivateLink) handoffs: we provide a private endpoint hostname that resolves to the customer's private link interface. We will provide the CIDR blocks used for the endpoint interfaces and the recommended allowlist for health checks.
- Health/telemetry ports: outbound 443 (TLS), 123 (NTP) for time sync in managed cases; we recommend allowing 10250-10255 for kubelet health where customers host probes (only if doing deep integration). I'll confirm the exact port list with infra.

I'll assemble: edge-nat-ip-list.csv, a network-diagram-v2.png, and a short signed note for the SIG pack. Targeting to send everything by EOD Tue so you have one day to review before Wed.

Looping in Laura (Network Security) and Vivek (Private Deployments) to validate the CIDRs and rotation policy.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: NAT IPs and private endpoint handover

Jordan / team — attaching the evidence pack for your SIG submission. Quick summary of the items included and answers to your clarifying questions are below.

Attachments:
- edge-nat-ip-list.csv (CSV) — list of stable egress NAT IP ranges (last updated 2026-08-05). Columns: range_start, range_end, region, purpose, rotation_window
- network-diagram-v2.png (PNG) — shows Acme VPC -> Redwood private endpoint -> ingress interface, labeled CIDRs used for endpoint interfaces and recommended allowlist on Acme side.
- signed-sig-responses.pdf (PDF) — short signed note confirming rotation policy and port list.

Answers to questions:
1) Ephemeral NAT rotations: In-flight sessions are preserved for TCP flows where a persistent connection exists; SNAT rotation is applied to new outbound sessions. There is no planned forced disconnect; we advertise rotation windows 72 hours in advance for any planned reassignments.
2) IPv6: At this time Redwood's private endpoint offering uses IPv4 A records for endpoint interfaces. We do not publish AAAA records for PrivateLink endpoints; IPv6 support for private endpoints is marked on our roadmap but not yet GA.
3) Ports/protocols: For the hosted API + private endpoint integration we require outbound HTTPS (443) from our infrastructure and allow inbound health checks on the following ports if the customer hosts probes: 443 (TLS), 8080 (optional app-level checks), and 10250-10255 (kubelet health probes; only when customer explicitly configures deep probe integration). We also recommend allowing outbound NTP (UDP/123) where we manage time sync.

Notes on CSV: ranges labelled "ephemeral" indicate blocks that may be rotated (weekly cadence) for load balancing. We include a rotation_window column with next planned rotation date when known.

If anything else is required for the SIG pack (signing on company letterhead, additional packet captures), reply and I will coordinate.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Network Security Lead, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: edge-nat-ip-list.csv (CSV), network-diagram-v2.png (PNG), signed-sig-responses.pdf (PDF)
